subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Laura — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our 30‑minute call so we have aligned next steps and success criteria. Please reply with any corrections.

TL;DR
- Primary goal: reduce production inference outages and improve graceful degradation (failover to cheaper models/regions) while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms for customer‑facing flows.
- Immediate ask: a short pilot to validate failover behavior + SLA targets for read‑only inference pipelines.

Pain points you shared
- Recent incident in June: single‑region GPU outage led to 2.5 hours of degraded responses (fallback to CPU caused latency spikes).
- No consistent multiregion failover policy — manual ops steps and data residency concerns.
- Concern about model quality vs. fallback correctness when routing to quantized/cheaper variants.

Current stack
- Frontend -> internal API gateway -> in‑house inference service (Kubernetes + mixed CPU/GPU nodes)
- Serving models: customer‑fine tuned LlamaX on GPU; fallback to CPU instance with 8GB quantized variant.

Success criteria (what FinServe told us)
1) Automated multiregion failover with RPO/RTO targets documented.
2) Canary + rollback for model variant fallbacks, with quality regression checks (pass/fail on defined prompts).
3) Maintain 95th pct latency < 300ms for core billing flows during steady state and < 700ms during controlled failover windows.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Redwood to send a one‑pager on reliability + proposed SLA options (attached). [Ben will include a reference SLA matrix and one‑pager].
- Joint scoping call with your Tech Ops (Jonas to lead) next week to map network topology and outage blast radius.
- Pilot: 2‑week proof‑of‑concept for multiregion failover using a staging traffic mirror (~5% traffic).

Open questions we need from you
- Can you share the incident postmortem for the June outage (redacted if needed)?
- Any hard constraints on data residency for cross‑region failover?
- Which 10 prompts would you like used for quality regression checks during pilot?

Attachments: redwood-reliability-one-pager.pdf, proposed-maup-sla.xlsx

Thanks again — I’ll schedule the scoping call once I hear back from your ops team on availability.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0122

Thanks Ben — this looks accurate and helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We can share a redacted postmortem for the June outage. Ops will send it by EOD Tuesday.
- Data residency: US only for production, but we can run staging failover in a neighboring US region.
- For the 10 prompts, I’ll pull a representative set from our billing flows and share by Wednesday.

Interested in the SLA matrix you mentioned — can you confirm whether the SLA would be for the hosted Redwood endpoint or for a Private deployment (customer‑managed)? We’re leaning towards Private for data controls but want to understand the tradeoffs w.r.t. failover behavior.

Laura Chen
Head of Product Ops | FinServe Inc.

Hi Laura — thanks for the fast response. Short answers: 

- SLA scope: we can propose two tracks in the matrix: Hosted Redwood (we manage routing + multiregion with our control plane) and Private (we ship a customer‑managed control plane with policies you define). The SLA numbers will differ: hosted typically allows tighter RTOs because we control routing and can failover across our fleet; Private gives you control and isolation but failover depends on your networking setup. I’ve attached the initial matrix.
- Pilot: Private staging looks reasonable — we'll set it up in a US secondary region and mirror ~5% of billing traffic.

Next steps (action items)
- Ben: schedule scoping call with Ops (Jonas) — proposed times Wed 9/9 10:00am PT or Thu 9/10 2:00pm PT.
- Laura/Ops: send redacted postmortem and prompt set.
- Marissa: draft a short runbook for the pilot including rollback triggers and regression thresholds.

I’ll drop a calendar invite once you confirm a time.

Best,
Ben

Quick internal note before I jump on the scoping call:

- I’ll draft a checklist for the network info we need from FinServe: VPC peering, egress IPs, region preferences, and whether they allow inter‑region traffic for staging.
- I’ll also prepare two example fallback configurations: (1) fall back to quantized variant in same region + autoscale CPU nodes, (2) failover to secondary region with lightweight model + prefix caching.
- Marissa — can you add the regression prompt set template to the Drive link and a short list of rollback triggers (latency > 700ms for 20m, error rate > 5% for 10m)?

I’ll be ready to lead the technical part of the call.
